people.paul.role: Writer in chains who thanks the Philippians for their gift
people.paul.relations: He writes with Timothy. Epaphroditus brought him the Philippians’ gift.
people.paul.meaning: Paul is in chains and does not know whether he will live or die. He says his chains have helped the Good News. He plans to send Timothy and Epaphroditus. He thanks the Philippians for the gift. He tells Euodia and Syntyche to agree.
people.jesus.role: Lord who humbled himself and was raised high
people.jesus.relations: Paul calls himself and Timothy servants of Jesus Christ. Paul says to have the mind that was in him.
people.jesus.meaning: Paul says Jesus took the form of a servant. He was obedient to death on a cross. Paul says God then raised him high. Every tongue will confess that he is Lord. Paul uses this to call the Philippians to humility.
people.timothy.role: Worker Paul hopes to send to Philippi
people.timothy.relations: He is named with Paul in the greeting. Paul says he served with him like a child with a father.
people.timothy.meaning: Paul hopes to send Timothy soon to learn how the Philippians are doing. Paul says no one else is so like-minded and truly cares about them. Paul says Timothy has proved himself. Paul will send him once he sees how things go.
people.epaphroditus.role: Philippian messenger who was nearly dead
people.epaphroditus.relations: Paul calls him brother, fellow worker, and fellow soldier. He brought the Philippians’ gift.
people.epaphroditus.meaning: Epaphroditus brought the Philippians’ gift to Paul. He fell sick nearly to death and longed for the Philippians. Paul sends him back. Paul asks them to receive him with joy and hold him in honor.
people.euodia.role: Fellow worker told to agree with Syntyche
people.euodia.relations: Paul names her with Syntyche. He asks a true partner to help both women.
people.euodia.meaning: Paul urges Euodia to think the same way as Syntyche in the Lord. He says both women labored with him in the Good News. The letter does not say what they disagree about.
people.syntyche.role: Fellow worker told to agree with Euodia
people.syntyche.relations: Paul names her with Euodia. He asks a true partner to help both women.
people.syntyche.meaning: Paul urges Syntyche to think the same way as Euodia in the Lord. He says both women labored with him in the Good News. The letter does not say what they disagree about.
places.philippi.summary: Paul writes in chapter 1 to the saints at Philippi, with the overseers and servants. In chapter 4 he calls them Philippians.
places.philippi.limits: The marker shows the city’s general location.
sources.web.summary: All four chapters are the main text for original close readings.
sources.web.limits: The guide did not check exact dates, the prison city, manuscripts, or Greek forms. It did not check who the rival workers were or why the two women disagree. The letter gives Paul’s view. It does not give a full reply from others.
sources.works-philippians.summary: Works reads joy in the middle of suffering and uncertain waiting.
sources.works-philippians.limits: This is Works’ own reading. The guide did not check her Greek analysis or her Roman setting. It did not check her wider account of peace. It did not review the linked works.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-42.summary: The lesson studies changed conduct and joy through Christ.
sources.cfm-nt-2023-42.limits: Philippians coverage follows what the lesson discusses in chapters two and four. The lesson title does not show coverage of every chapter. The guide did not check the linked talks, videos, or Restoration passages.
sources.atlas-canaan.summary: This Church-published atlas names towns and regions in Canaan.
sources.atlas-canaan.limits: It supplies only the chosen reference coordinates. The earlier review record is unchanged. This source does not confirm Gospel events or exact routes.
sources.net-acts-map.summary: Opening descriptions and coordinates mark the cities named in Acts.
sources.net-acts-map.limits: These broad points do not confirm ancient events, travel paths, buildings, or coastlines. The guide did not adopt older encyclopedia claims about authorship, law, population, or exact dates.
chapters.*.mapNote: The map marks Philippi as one city point. It shows no prison or home.
chapters.*.routeEvidence: The letter gives no delivery route and does not name the prison city.
